headline: Sequence-Based Prediction of Dynamic Protein Properties Under Systematic Evaluation
label: Protein Property Prediction Benchmarks
summary: Systematic benchmarks now test sequence-based predictors of phase separation, disorder, and cryptic pockets against diverse datasets and MD references.
synthesis: The dominant thread is deep learning prediction of protein properties beyond static folds, including phase separation, intrinsic disorder, conformational flexibility, mutational energetic frustration, and cryptic pocket opening. A systematic evaluation of nine LLPS predictors reports context-dependent performance across IDR, folded, mutant, and viral datasets. A cryptic pocket benchmark finds AI ensemble methods fast but qualitative relative to MD simulations, which remain quantitatively predictive. Mutant kcat analysis attributes prediction accuracy largely to enzyme-group activity ranges and shared mutation directions, motivating a bias-aware pairwise approach. ProtProfileMD learns MD-derived flexibility from sequence by finetuning ProstT5, and UdonPred applies ProstT5 embeddings to disorder prediction. What is new is the shift toward dataset-aware and simulation-referenced assessment of sequence-based and pLM-derived predictors.
